question: Who was the President of India between the years 1987 and 1992?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R Venkataraman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **R Venkataraman** served as the 8th President of India from **25 July 1987 to 25 July 1992**.
 
• He was elected as President by the **Electoral College of India**, consisting of elected members of both houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• Prior to his presidency, Venkataraman held significant positions, including **Vice President of India** and **Minister of Defence**.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in 1988 for his services to the nation.
 
• Venkataraman played a crucial role in India’s political landscape during his tenure, emphasizing stability and constitutional values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electoral College**

 
 
• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The election follows the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The process ensures uniformity in representation of different states.
 
 
 
• **Vice President of India**
 
 
• The Vice President is the second-highest constitutional office in India, succeeding the President.
 
• The Vice President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• The term of the Vice President is five years, and they can be re-elected.
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan**
 
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service in any field including government service.
 
• The awards are announced every year on Republic Day (26th January).
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Values**
 
 
• Constitutional values refer to the fundamental principles and ideals upon which the Indian Constitution is based.
 
• These include justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Presidents of India play a crucial role in upholding these values through their office and actions.
